prompt: Implement ScoreBumper: bumpInPlace changes the caller's own array, bumpedCopy returns a brand new array and leaves the original alone, and sameArray compares references with == rather than contents.
explanation: An array parameter is a copy of a reference, not a copy of the array, so writing scores[i] inside a method is visible to the caller. Building a new array and returning it gives the caller a second, independent object -- the original keeps its values. == on arrays asks whether two references point at the same object, which is why two arrays holding identical numbers are still not the same array.
hints: bumpInPlace returns nothing: it walks the indexes and writes each bumped value back into the very array the caller passed in.
bumpedCopy needs 'new int[scores.length]' (or Arrays.copyOf) before it fills anything in.
sameArray is literally 'return a == b;' -- that also gives the right answer when both are null.
